title: Write draft-atwood-mimi-catchup: the wire half of follower catch-up
description:
Answers Mark's question (2026-11-26): should jump and fill detection go
in the I-D, and which I-D?

## Which I-D: a new one

A new individual draft, draft-atwood-mimi-catchup, in its own repo
~/PROJECT/ietf-mimi-catchup, laid out like ietf-mimi-calls and
ietf-mimi-provider-auth (.md, .xml, README.md).

Not an edit to draft-ietf-mimi-protocol: that is a WG document, and the
catchUp endpoint would be an eleventh endpoint beside its §5.1 ten. The
established mimid pattern for "we have a mechanism the WG does not" is a
draft-atwood-* individual draft, which then proposes adoption or a PR
against protocol. Not mimi-arch (architecture, not mechanism) and not
mimi-content (nothing to do with message content).

## Normative: the wire, and the two properties the local half needs

- The per-room fanout sequence: assigned by the hub, per room, from 1,
  by one, never reused and never renumbered.
- Where it travels: beside the message, not inside FanoutMessage
  (decision mimid-1wgh.104), so an implementation that does not know it
  is unaffected and a proxy cannot strip it unnoticed. mimid puts it in
  the `mimi-fanout-sequence` header and covers it in the RFC 9421
  signature.
- The catchUp endpoint: the request (the sequence held, and a limit),
  the answer (fanouts in hub order, each carrying its sequence, plus the
  hub's current highest), and the directory member that advertises it.
  Publishing the member IS the capability negotiation, which is what
  makes it safe to add with no version number.
- The distinct refusal when the range is older than the hub holds: it
  MUST be distinguishable and MUST NOT be answered with the oldest still
  held, which would look complete and hide the loss.
- Retention bounds catch-up, stated so the two cannot drift.
- THE TWO PROPERTIES, which are the real answer to Mark's question.
  Without them another implementation breaks the local half silently:
  1. every fanout of a room goes to every provider then in the room, so
     a destination's received sequences are contiguous. In mimid this is
     an accident of how `destinations` is built (hub/update.rs takes the
     union of the domains before and after; the BYTES differ per
     destination, the set does not), not a stated rule. A hub that
     fanned out to a subset would give every follower false gaps.
  2. a hub serves catch-up contiguously from what was asked, for that
     requester. Follower::fill_gap relies on it to know a gap is closed.

## NOT normative: jump and fill detection

Jump detection, the fill loop and its stopping rule, the probe and its
interval, and the per-room in-flight guard are all local policy. A
follower may notice a gap however it likes, or never notice one and only
probe (decision mimid-1wgh.37.104.11). They belong in an implementation
-considerations section as guidance, if at all -- describing them
normatively would over-specify a receiver's bookkeeping.

The honest framing: the draft must make the local half POSSIBLE (the two
properties above) without mandating how it is done.

## Constraint: no JMAP, at all

AGENTS.md: never mention JMAP in anything sent to the MIMI WG. That
bites here, because mimid's surfacing half IS JMAP -- the
follower_room.gone count, RFC 8620 §5.6 cannotCalculateChanges, a client
resyncing (decision mimid-1wgh.37.104.8). None of that can appear.

State the requirement protocol-neutrally instead: a follower MUST be
able to tell its own users that a range of a room's history is
permanently missing, and MUST NOT present a room as complete when it is
not. How it tells them is out of scope.

## Evidence to cite

The chairs have been gated on implementation evidence since the
2026-01-13 chair message. There is now running code: f4a1b9c6 (both
halves), 670dd315 (two providers, a real gap recovered, and the
unfillable case reported). Still only mimid talking to mimid, which the
draft should say rather than imply interop.

Do not send anything upstream without Mark's OK (memory:
dont-flood-upstream).
close_reason: Written and committed in ~/PROJECT/ietf-mimi-catchup (e854a41, 5f0457f, e130af5, eac9a48), builds clean at 18 pages. Normative: the per-room sequence, the mimi-fanout-sequence header, the catchUp operation and its response codes, the distinct out-of-window refusal, retention, and the two properties the local half depends on. Non-normative: detection, filling, probing. Section 9 carries replacement text for protocol-07 section 5.5. No JMAP anywhere in it (AGENTS.md). Not submitted; the repo has no remote yet.
